findings.issue: The spec (A-4) only says to prevent `cancel`. The extra onKeyDown handler that blocks Escape is justified, because Chromium's close-watcher closes a modal on a second Escape without user activation and does not fire a cancellable `cancel`. But nothing says so, and a reader may remove it as a duplicate.
findings.evidence: onCancel={(event) => event.preventDefault()} and onKeyDown={(event) => { if (event.key === 'Escape') event.preventDefault(); }}
findings.fix: Add a one-line comment above onKeyDown explaining that it covers repeated Escape, which Chromium's close watcher otherwise closes without a cancellable cancel event.

summary: All 17 SPEC items are implemented as specified. The headless rules (userBusted, rebuy, the 'rebuy' step, the dealHand guard, nextHandDelay returning null, the nextHand $0 branch placed before the untouched TEMPORARY line), the record changes (rebuys written, restored and capped, the user-$0 exemption for cash only) and the UI (native modal dialog, hidden while a review is held, the rebuy action waiting on the write) all match. The tests assert the specified values and errors, cover the sit-and-go, bot-on-0 and mid-hand all-in edges, and use the hook's own pure updaters (dealAfterDone, rebuyAndDeal), so a broken hook rule would fail them. The new vitest files pass locally (15/15), and the gate run fix-2 passes. The three recorded deviations are all acceptable. (1) The session.acceptance.test.ts change only widens a type annotation, as NextStep requires. (2) Switching the button check to config.seats is needed because the busted user seat is no longer in the chips list. It behaves the same, since the record's seats are already checked to equal config.seats in order. (3) The next-hand.test.ts re-pin changes only the expected value for userStack 0, with the same number of checks. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings; one MINOR comment reflow and one NIT.
